 Intel cuts more jobs as CEO Lip-Bu Tan's efficiency push continues

 After a series of layoffs over the last two years, Intel has let workers go again in another round of cuts, Business Insider has learned.
 The cuts are the latest sign that CEO Lip-Bu Tan's effort to make the chipmaker leaner is continuing into the final months of the year.
 This week, some employees posted on social media about being affected by layoffs in Intel's global IT workforce.
 "As part of our broader strategy to become a more focused and efficient company, we continually assess our workforce to ensure priorities and resources are appropriately aligned," an Intel spokesperson said in a statement.
 Intel did not disclose how many employees were affected or identify the teams involved.
 Have a tip? Contact Alice via email at atecotzky@insider.com or Signal at alicetecotzky.05. Contact Shuby at sgoel@insider.com or Signal at shuby.85. Use a personal email address and a nonwork device; here's our guide to sharing information securely .
 The job cuts add to a lengthy restructuring at the US chipmaker, which has reduced its workforce and trimmed projects as it tries to revive its business after years of manufacturing setbacks and market share losses in AI chips. 
 Intel's share price has taken a beating in recent months, down about 60% since the end of June. Since the start of the year, though, it's up nearly 50%. 
 Tan, who became Intel's CEO last year, has said his restructuring plan is designed to lower expenses, reduce management layers, and shift resources away from lower-priority initiatives.
 Intel employed 81,100 people at the end of September, down from 85,100 at the end of 2025, according to company filings.

 Its headcount has fallen sharply since 2024, when Intel announced plans to cut more than 15,000 jobs, or about 15% of its workforce, under then-CEO Pat Gelsinger .
 Other tech companies have also laid off staff this year, including Amazon, Meta, and Salesforce . Some, like Block , have explicitly cited AI, as the technology continues to transform how businesses operate.
